ai.summary: Nvidia’s board said it is opening an independent investigation into reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted in a foreign intelligence effort. The company said it has no reason to believe Nvidia secrets or national-security information were compromised; China called the allegations baseless.
ai.title: China dismisses a spy plot claim involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang as smear campaign

ai.summary: The U.S. government unit responsible for assessing AI safety reportedly lacks a permanent leader, has stopped publishing research, and was asked to informally report to a White House office. Former officials and critics raised concerns that the arrangement could undermine the center’s independence.
ai.title: Staff at the US center for AI safety are reporting to the White House, raising independence concerns

quantum.summary: IBM and public-sector partners announced the company’s first Illinois deployment of a Quantum System Two, powered by its Nighthawk chip. The system is intended to support research into quantum algorithms and applications, with plans to move it to the Illinois Quantum and Microelectronics Park.
quantum.title: IBM Deploys First Quantum Computer in Illinois with Quantum System Two

quantum.summary: IBM, Oak Ridge National Laboratory and AMD announced a quantum-classical co-design effort focused on error correction, pairing IBM quantum hardware with Oak Ridge computing resources. The project targets the substantial classical processing needed to decode errors in quantum systems.
quantum.title: IBM, Oak Ridge and AMD launch quantum error-correction co-design platform

quantum.summary: Horizon Quantum and OQC announced pulse-level integration of OQC’s 32-qubit Toshiko processor with Horizon’s Triple Alpha development environment. The integration gives developers access to hardware controls for characterization and gate calibration alongside application development.
quantum.title: Horizon Quantum and OQC Announce Successful Pulse-Level Integration

quantum.summary: Quantum X Labs reported preliminary benchmarks showing up to 20% fewer logical decoding failures after applying its noise-model calibration approach to data from three IBM processors. The company described the results as early tests, not a demonstration of fault-tolerant computation.
quantum.title: Quantum X Labs Expands AI-Powered Quantum Error Correction Program to Three IBM Quantum Processors

quantum.summary: Quantum Transportation, a Rail Vision subsidiary, said it began error-correction experiments on the Arbel superconducting processor at the Israeli Quantum Computing Center. The initial work links device characterization, circuit execution and decoding; the announcement explicitly says it does not yet demonstrate real-time error correction or fault tolerance.
quantum.title: Rail Vision’s Quantum Platform Launches End-to-End Quantum Error Correction Program
